title: Universal operadic algebra fibration and fixed-operad limits
statement: Use the infinity-category, universe, and presentably monoidal conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the accessibility/presentability conventions of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and the fibration conventions of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. A base map is inert when its opposite includes a consecutive subinterval; an edge of an operad over such a map is inert only when it is cocartesian. A nonsymmetric infinity operad is an inner fibration $\mathcal O^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ such that every inert arrow has a cocartesian lift, the Segal map $\mathcal O_{[n]}\to\mathcal O_{[1]}^n$ induced by the inert maps is an equivalence for every $[n]$, and, for every $C\in\mathcal O_{[n]}$ with chosen cocartesian inert lifts $C\to C_i$ over the maps $\rho_i:[n]\to[1]$, $C$ is the $\pi$-limit of the $C_i$; equivalently, for every $X\in\mathcal O_{[m]}$ and $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, the mapping-space map $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}_{\mathcal O^\otimes}(X,C)\to\prod_i\operatorname{Map}^{\rho_i\circ\phi}_{\mathcal O^\otimes}(X,C_i)$ is an equivalence. Here $\operatorname{Map}^{\phi}$ is the homotopy fiber of the map on mapping spaces over the base arrow $\phi$. Write $\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$ for the infinity category of small such operads and inert-preserving functors over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. For a presentably monoidal $\mathcal V$, let $\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)$ be the Cartesian unstraightening of the coherent functor $\mathcal O\mapsto\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal V)$ with restriction transports. Then the projection $\pi:\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)\to\operatorname{Opd}^{\mathrm{ns}}_\infty$ is both a Cartesian and a coCartesian fibration: its Cartesian transport along $u:\mathcal O\to\mathcal P$ is restriction $u^*$, and its coCartesian transport is the operadic free extension $u_!\dashv u^*$. The base and total infinity categories are presentable and $\pi$ is accessible, where accessible for a functor means preservation of small $\kappa$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$ (and accessible/presentable categories have the meanings in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]). Here an algebra is an inert-preserving functor over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$. A generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad is an inner fibration satisfying (i) inert cocartesian lifts, (ii) the Segal equivalence $\mathcal M_{[n]}\simeq\mathcal M_{[1]}\times_{\mathcal M_{[0]}}\cdots\times_{\mathcal M_{[0]}}\mathcal M_{[1]}$ (the zero-factor fiber product for $n=0$ is $\mathcal M_{[0]}$), and (iii) the following incidence-diagram axiom. Let $I_n$ be the category of all inert maps $\alpha:[n]\to[i]$, $i\in\{0,1\}$, with morphisms the commuting triangles of inert maps between their targets. For each $C\in\mathcal M_{[n]}$, choose the cocartesian inert projection diagram $(C_\alpha)_{\alpha\in I_n}$. For every $X\in\mathcal M_{[m]}$ and base arrow $\phi:[m]\to[n]$, the canonical map $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}^{\phi}(X,C)\to\lim_{\alpha\in I_n}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal M}^{\alpha\phi}(X,C_\alpha)$ is an equivalence; require $\mathcal M_{[0]}$ to be a Kan complex. For every small generalized nonsymmetric infinity operad $\mathcal M$ with Kan space $\mathcal M_{[0]}$, $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$ is presentable. Its small limits are created by restriction to the inert part (the wide subcategory of arrows lying over inert base maps, with its cocartesian inert edges still required to be preserved), and are computed pointwise on colors: $\operatorname{ev}_c(\lim_j B_j)\simeq\lim_j\operatorname{ev}_c(B_j)$ for $c\in\mathcal M_{[1]}$. In particular, restriction along a map of generalized operads preserves small limits.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.11 (universal algebra fibration); Section 3.2 (operad category); Corollary A.5.7 (fixed generalized operad); operadic limits as in Higher Algebra, Proposition 3.2.2.1 and Corollaries 3.2.2.3–3.2.2.5. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Fix the universes, presentably monoidal $\mathcal V$, accessibility and fibration conventions of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category] and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. The ordinary and generalized operad axioms in the statement are the respective definitions: the former has terminal zero-fiber, the latter has the incidence diagram of inert maps to both $[0]$ and $[1]$. An algebra preserves the chosen inert cocartesian edges. Precomposition along an inert-preserving operad map therefore gives a functor of algebra infinity categories, coherently on strings of maps. For existence of the stipulated Cartesian unstraightening apply [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] in a containing universe to the functor $\mathcal O\mapsto\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal V)^{\mathrm{op}}$ on the opposite operad base. Take the opposite of its cocartesian total category. The result is Cartesian over the operad base, has fibers $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal V)$, and Cartesian transport $u^*$: taking opposites reverses the cocartesian lifting conditions and the transport arrows. The classification equivalence and base-change compatibility give the coherent restriction functor, so this realizes the specified total category.

Let $\mathcal M$ be small generalized with Kan $\mathcal M_{[0]}$. Apply [lem-coef-generalized-operadic-monadicity]: restriction to colors is monadic over $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal M_{[1]},\mathcal V)$, its source has sifted colimits and it preserves them. The color category is small since $\mathcal M$ is small. By [lem-coef-infinity-monadic-sifted-presentability] its functor category into presentable $\mathcal V$ is presentable, and the same node's monadic clause gives presentability of $\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal M}(\mathcal V)$. Thus the fixed-operad assertion has been derived from monadicity and a general presentability theorem, rather than renamed as a new lemma. Ordinary operads are included, since their zero-fibers are contractible.

source.place: Proof of Corollary A.5.7 via Corollary A.5.6, Lemma A.5.8 and Proposition A.5.9.

proof.text: The underlying $\mathcal V$ has small limits by [lem-coef-accessible-infinity-pullback]. Under the monoidal Segal equivalence of [def-coef-complete-algebroid], the fiber of $\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $[n]$ is $\mathcal V^n$. For an inert map $[n]\to[m]$, transport is the projection to the indicated consecutive $m$ entries, hence preserves all small limits, including terminal objects and the map to $\mathcal V^0\simeq *$. Apply [lem-coef-marked-sections-pointwise-limits] with $S=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$, $E=\mathcal V^\otimes$, $T=\mathcal M$, and $W$ the inert edges of $\mathcal M$. Its marked sections are exactly $\mathcal M$-algebras. It supplies limits on the same objects as fiberwise limits in $\operatorname{Fun}_{\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}}(\mathcal M,\mathcal V^\otimes)$ and says that fiberwise evaluation detects limit cones. An algebra's value at an object over $[n]$ is its ordered $n$-tuple of inert color values; the value over $[0]$ is in a terminal fiber. Therefore the criterion reduces to the color evaluations, giving $\operatorname{ev}_c(\lim_jB_j)\simeq\lim_jB_j(c)$. Apply the marked-section theorem also with $T=\mathcal M_{\mathrm{triv}}$, the wide subcategory of all arrows lying over inert base maps, with $W$ still the cocartesian inert edges. This retains the possibly noninvertible arrows in the color category; those arrows are not required to become cocartesian. A limiting cone there is colorwise limiting. The limiting algebra cone already constructed restricts to another limit cone on the same inert diagram. The universal property gives an equivalence of these two cones, including their projections; composing that equivalence with the constructed algebra cone lifts the specified inert cone up to the contractible choice of a limit. Every algebra cone restricting to it is colorwise limiting and therefore limiting. This is creation of limits in the infinity-categorical sense. This argument uses only a cocartesian fibration and inert projections, so applies to generalized nonsymmetric operads without any passage from $\mathrm{Fin}_*$ to $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$.

source.place: Agent marked-section argument; compare HA Section 3.2.2, with the symmetric-operad proposition not applied directly.

proof.text: For a map $u:\mathcal M\to\mathcal N$, evaluation of the restricted algebra at any color $c$ is evaluation of the original algebra at $u(c)$. Thus restricting a colorwise limiting cone gives another colorwise limiting cone. The criterion in step 3 makes it a limit cone of $\mathcal M$-algebras. This proves preservation of all small limits, also for a map changing colors and for the empty diagram.

The category of ordinary small operads is presentable by [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operads-presentability]. Its objects have exactly the three ordinary axioms in step 1; in particular the smallness universe is the same as the one used for $\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)$. This is the base presentability required below, not a consequence of the definition of presentability.

source.place: Section 3.2, opening paragraph, Corollary 3.2.6 and Definition 3.2.7.

proof.text: Fix a map $u:\mathcal O\to\mathcal P$ of ordinary small operads. For any color $b$ of $\mathcal P$, the active comma category $K_b$ of [lem-coef-operadic-active-colimit-extension-criterion] is small: it is a fiber product of a wide subcategory and a slice of small operads. For every algebra $A$, its tensor diagram $D_{A,b}$ therefore has a colimit in $\mathcal V$. For fixed $L,R$, first tensoring on the left by $L$ and then on the right by $R$ preserves every small colimit by presentable monoidality in [def-coef-complete-algebroid]. Their composite $x\mapsto L\otimes x\otimes R$ therefore preserves this particular colimit, as the criterion requires. Taking either object to be the unit also covers one-sided and empty contexts. The criterion gives the coherent adjunction $u_!\dashv u^*$, with its operadic colimit formula and unit. This proves existence of the needed coCartesian transport without citing the downstream operadic-free-extension node, whose statement depends on this item.

source.place: Propositions A.2.10 and A.4.3-A.4.4, Corollary A.4.5; the construction used in Theorem A.4.6.

proof.text: For $A$ over $\mathcal O$ take the edge over $u$ from $A$ to $u_!A$ specified by its adjunction unit $A\to u^*u_!A$. For $C$ over $\mathcal Q$, consider the comparison induced by precomposition with this chosen edge from $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)}(u_!A,C)$ to the homotopy pullback $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)}(A,C)\times^h_{\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Opd}}(\mathcal O,\mathcal Q)}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Opd}}(\mathcal P,\mathcal Q)$. Both spaces map to the SAME base $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Opd}}(\mathcal P,\mathcal Q)$. Over $v:\mathcal P\to\mathcal Q$ their fibers are respectively $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal P}}(u_!A,v^*C)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}}(A,u^*v^*C)$, as follows from the Cartesian lifts. For the Cartesian lift $v^*C\to C$ (and the lift of $vu$), apply [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] to its opposite. Take the fiber over the identity of the source base object in that homotopy-pullback square. It identifies maps in the fiber into the lifted object with the homotopy fiber over $v$ (respectively $vu$) of the total mapping space. This proves the displayed identifications, including their coherent dependence on $v$. For a fiber map $h:u_!A\to v^*C$, this comparison is $h\mapsto u^*(h)\circ\eta_A$, where $\eta_A:A\to u^*u_!A$ is the adjunction unit. This is exactly the adjunction equivalence of step 6, naturally in $v,C$. The square throughout is the coherent precomposition square stipulated by [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion], including its composition data, rather than a square equipped with an independently chosen commutation homotopy. Naturality of the unit and restriction identifies these fiber maps with its comparison. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] to this comparison over the IDENTITY of its base (hence a base equivalence). It is an equivalence, so the original mapping-space square is homotopy Cartesian. The horn-to-mapping-square equivalence in [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] now makes the chosen edge cocartesian. Hence these edges give all cocartesian lifts, and the coCartesian transport is $u_!$. This identifies the transport variance explicitly.

Write $G(\mathcal O)=\operatorname{Alg}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal V)$. The tensor and right-adjoint equivalence of [lem-coef-nonsymmetric-operadic-tensor-adjunction] gives, for a small diagram $(\mathcal O_j)_{j\in J}$ of operads and any test infinity category $C$ in a containing universe,
$$\operatorname{Map}(C,G(\operatorname{colim}_j\mathcal O_j))\simeq\operatorname{Map}(C\odot\operatorname{colim}_j\mathcal O_j,\mathcal V^\otimes)\simeq\operatorname{Map}(\operatorname{colim}_j(C\odot\mathcal O_j),\mathcal V^\otimes)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(C\odot\mathcal O_j,\mathcal V^\otimes)\simeq\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}(C,G(\mathcal O_j)).$$
Here the tensor node's universe-enlargement clause identifies the small-operad colimit with the same colimit in the containing universe. The middle equivalence then uses preservation of colimits by the tensor, and the next one is the mapping-space universal property of a colimit in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Equivalently this says that the restriction cone of algebra categories is limiting, by the mapping-space limit criterion in that same node, tested on all $C$ in the larger universe. Thus $G$ carries small colimits in operads to limits of infinity categories. In particular it carries small $\kappa$-filtered colimits in operads to limits over the opposite indexing category, for any infinite regular $\kappa$. All the comparisons are natural in the operad diagram, rather than merely bijections in a homotopy category.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 3.6.8, with the categorical-pattern tensor made explicit.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presentable-cartesian-fibration] to the stipulated Cartesian algebra fibration. Its base is presentable by step 5, its fibers by step 2, its Cartesian restrictions are right adjoints by step 6, and its classifying functor carries sufficiently filtered colimits in the base to limits by step 8. These are all of that node's hypotheses. It follows that $\operatorname{Alg}(\mathcal V)$ is presentable and its projection is accessible. Combined with steps 1 and 7 this proves the universal fibration assertions, and steps 2-4 prove the fixed generalized-operad assertions.
